SC6_mentions.result: NOT IMPLEMENTED — recorded as a follow-up slice, per the decision rule
SC6_mentions.finding: Mention notifications are not a shipped capability. vidra-user's 'mention' is a client-DERIVED attribution prefix: lib/comments.ts replyMention reads parent_id against the already-loaded comment list and renders a plain, non-linked '@handle' before a nested reply's body (CommentsSection). There is no autocomplete picker, no 'mention someone' affordance, no linkification of handles typed into a comment body, and no promise of delivery. vidra-core has no mention feature at all. Building one would mean a parser, a resolution rule, an abuse story and a new notification type — deliberately NOT widened into this PR.

implementation_notes.no_migration: notifications.type is unconstrained TEXT (migration 0018, restated by 0103), so a new type needs no schema change. Latest migration remains 0127.
implementation_notes.selection_rules_live_in_sql: One new :one query, CommentReplyRecipient, following the 0101/0103 set-based idiom: local parent author only (a federated parent has NULL user_id per 0053), no tombstones (0057), no self-notification, active non-deleted account, mute and block excluded in both directions.
implementation_notes.mutual_exclusion: handleCreateComment resolves the reply recipient FIRST and skips the owner's 'comment' notification only when the video's owner IS that recipient.
implementation_notes.best_effort_preserved: Both notifications remain best-effort side effects: a failure is logged and never fails the comment.

deep_link_limitation: A reply notification links to the video, not to the comment. There is no per-comment anchor anywhere in vidra-user, and replies render inside a collapsed 'View N replies' control, so a #comment-<id> fragment would target a node that is not in the DOM. Deep-linking a notification to the exact comment needs anchors plus auto-expansion of the containing thread — recorded as the next slice, not built here.
unrelated_findings: NotifyComment (the video-owner notification) does NOT consult mutes or blocks: an account the owner has muted or blocked still reaches the owner's inbox by commenting on their video. The new reply path excludes them; the older owner path was left exactly as it was rather than silently changing behaviour under an unrelated slice.

The frontend's Notification type is a generated string union, so a backend type with no UI case falls through describeNotification's final return and renders as 'started following your channel'. NotificationPrefsView degrades safely (unknown keys render raw), but the Inbox does not — a default arm that renders something neutral would turn this class of bug from wrong into merely plain.
